utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Madam Registrar. Could you kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam. All the accused are here. Again, if you have any problems with interpretation, please draw my attention straight away. Defence teams are all here, only noticeable or conspicuous absence is Mr. Bourgon. We will have less objections today. Prosecution, that's Mr. Vanderpuye and Mr. McCloskey. The witness is already in his place. Good morning to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Last Friday, I explained to you the protective measures which have been put in place for your benefit so that you can testify without any background worries in your mind and you can testify with more tranquillity. You also made a -- took a solemn undertaking with us that you will testify the truth. Mr. Vanderpuye and the registrar have made available over the weekend a copy of the transcript of your previous testimony, which we have carefully perused. I take it that you will proceed with reading out a brief summary of that testimony now, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: With the Court's permission, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And it could well be that after reading out this summary, Mr. Vanderpuye might have some more questions for you. After that, I will hand you over to the seven defence teams for the cross-examination. Thank you, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, good morning, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Rather than lose time, I was just checking because my memory failed me, whether last Friday we dealt with the foundation issues, in other words, whether you asked the witness if he had gone through -- yes. In fact we had also the question of how he went through it, the translation, yeah, okay. All right. Make sure that the requirements of the provision of Rule 92 ter are fully met, fully observed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Last Friday, Mr. Witness, there seemed to be some confusion with respect to the documents that you reviewed and I wanted to ask some questions just to clarify the record. I believe you initially indicated that you had had an interpreter read back to you your prior testimony in the matter of Prosecutor versus Krstic in which you testified on the 23rd of May of 2000. Do you recall -- do you recall testifying in that manner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And was that the case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You also indicated that you had read certain documents on your own without the benefit of an interpreter. Is that the case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not the case. Things were misinterpreted to me. And I apologise to the Trial Chamber. It was in English. The interpreter interpreted things to me. I spotted a few errors that I corrected and that was that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I'd asked you also on Friday whether or not, having reviewed your prior testimony in the other trial, whether or not were questions to be put to you regarding that testimony you would answer the same way as if you were examined here today. Is that the case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would offer at this time the prior transcript -- the prior testimony of PW-112 in evidence at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Any objections from the Defence teams? I wouldn't imagine so. So, yes, it is so admitted pursuant to Rule 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you. Just so the record is clear, I'm referring to Exhibit P02272, which is the transcript, as I understand it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's a new document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. One moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I think if I remember well, even last time, Mr. Vanderpuye himself hinted that it should be so. I think it needs to be kept under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, please, Judge. And I would also ask that the exhibits that are attendant to that testimony be admitted as well as integral to that testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you better specify them at some point in time either during the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. That would be a good time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: May I proceed with the summary?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This will be under seal and please go through the documents that are attached to it to make sure that what needs to be under seal will remain under seal, all right? What need not be under seal will retain public. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: "1. Witness PW-112 lived in Srebrenica with his wife, two children in July 1995. Prior to the arrival of UNPROFOR forces, PW-112 acknowledged that a Territorial Defence existed in the protected area, of which PW-112 had been formally a member. Until about a year before the war, PW-112 had good relations with Serbs which had since deteriorated. "2. On 11 July 1995, PW-112 was forced to separate from his family because of the advance of Serb forces who had, by that date, "Taken over half the town from the hill of Bojna." That's a reference to transcript page 3239, lines 23 through 24. "The decision was made to separate at that time because PW-112 saw there was no possibility of safety in remaining any longer. "3. At around 2.30 p.m., PW-112 left Srebrenica together with several men towards the village of Slatine and Susnjari while his family went to Potocari. PW-112 estimates that the men gathered at Susnjari at the time of his arrival (about 10 p.m.) numbered around 12.000 to 15.000 with, approximately one-third lightly armed with hunting rifles and other types of small arms. PW-112 himself had a grenade which he intended to commit suicide with if captured. "4. PW-112 together with several men left Susnjari at around midnight on 11th of July going into the 12th, following an informal gathering with the other men. During this gathering, the men were lined up and those with weapons were interspersed among those unarmed to better protect lives against likely ambushes and men were lined up so that as many people could cross the nearby Serb lines as possible. "5. Among the people leading this group were, "The head of the municipality, those in charge of civilian authority, and some others who were in Srebrenica in the course of the war, the chiefs of some secretariats, for example." There were also some "Territorial Defence" people there." And that's a reference to transcript page 3242, line 1 through 4. "6. On the 12th of July 1995, from about 5 a.m. until 11.30 a.m., PW-112 was at Buljim in front of the first Serb lines, the column of men had been interrupted. Shortly after 11.30 a.m., PW-112 crossed Serb lines together with a group of men. The group encountered a Serb ambush thereafter near a stream. "7. PW-112 escaped the ambush reaching Kamenica hill and catching up with part of the column that had preceded his group across Serb lines. There the men were reorganised and proceeded toward the village of Kamenica where they arrived that evening. The group then moved on to the village of Burnice arriving there at about midnight on the night of 12th July. PW-112 fell asleep or lost consciousness shortly thereafter. "8. At around 3 a.m. on 13th July, PW-112 awoke finding himself alone. The witness was in a "grassland and then went into a corn field." Referring to transcript page 3244 line 21. "At this point, PW-112 referred to Exhibit in the prior matter, Exhibit number 176 which was a map indicating the position between Kravica and Rijeka about a kilometre south of Konjevic Polje." "9. Having some familiarity with the area and recognising a bridge going towards Kasaba, PW-112 proceeded down towards the Kravica River ("the river which flows from the Kravica direction and it flows under the bridge and joins up with the Jadar River." Transcript page 3245, lines 1 through 3. "From the bridge, PW-112 decided not to attempt to cross the river and went back to the corn field. "10. While in the corn field, PW-112 heard the sound of people closeby and tried to avoid being seen by going into a partially burned down house. In doing so, PW-112 stepped on a broken roof tile and was detected. Following shots above his head, PW-112 was directed to surrender by police in dark blue camouflage uniforms. PW-112 recognised one of the policemen. "11. Following his surrender, one of the first things taken from PW-112 was his identification. His wallet, diary, telephone directory and money were taken from his person. Also taken was the grenade contained in his bag. PW-112 was then ordered by one of the policemen to, "lie down so I can slit your throat." Referring to transcript page 3247, lines 21 through 22. "Though he complied, a second policeman whom PW-112 also recognised, directed that he be left alone. Thereafter, PW-112 was taken by this policeman to an area in front of a school in which there were a couple of soldiers in camouflage uniforms guarding a shed (a small building). At this point the witness referred to Exhibit 177 depicting a small shed indicating that he entered this little brick building in the front and from the right side. "12. Inside the shed, PW-112 recognised two individuals, both Muslim captives. From the shed, PW-112 was taken across a meadow to another house for questioning. Together with the other captives, PW-112 was taken to a house in front of which four men in military camouflage uniforms were sitting around a table. The witness did not see any insignia. At this point in his testimony the witness referred to Exhibit number 178, indicating a building in front of which there was a tree. "13. Between approximately 7 and 9 a.m., PW-112 was questioned. During the questioning, PW-112 was not beaten and received something to eat and drink. During the questioning, PW-112 was told by one of the questioners who identified himself as Cica that he had been in command of the operation on Srebrenica in 1993 in the year of Kragljivoda and Osmace. Following this, PW-112 was directed along with the other captives to take notice of 12 buses which had come by with women and children on board. At this time, one of the soldiers commented, "You see how respectful they (referring to the soldiers) were of us (referring to the Muslims) that they didn't force too many people on to the buses but only as many as could sit down." Referring to transcript page 3258, lines 8 through 10. "The statement was acknowledged by PW-112. "A short while after this exchange, PW-112 was directed to another house in front of the one where the questioning occurred. "14. This house was empty and PW-112 and the other captives were held on the ground floor. Later, a 14 to 15 year old boy was brought in. He was subsequently taken into the hallway and beaten and then brought back. After a while, and over a period of time, three men were brought in, one of whom was known to PW-112. Thereafter, a Serb man known to PW-112 came in, directing and accompanying PW-112 and two other men and the young boy to a warehouse near the banks of the Jadar river. "15. The warehouse was a location that PW-112 knew to be an agricultural chemist where medicines for agricultural purposes could be purchased. When PW-112 arrived at the warehouse, he recognised another of his captives. Upon entering, PW-112 was taken to the smaller of two rooms. Inside there were men in military camouflage uniforms armed with rifles and automatic weapons. These men directed PW-112, as well as the other men, to remove their clothes. Thereafter, together with the other men, he was lined up against a wall and beaten. In addition to PW-112 and the other -- and the two men and the boy that accompanied him, 12 other individuals were lined up and beaten. "16. Later on PW-112 and the other men were told to get dressed and were subsequently transferred to a larger room. This was the former public part of the agricultural shop. The men were again lined up prone against a wall and beaten with batons. Following this, a bus driver -- a bus driven by a blond woman parked in front of the warehouse. PW-112 was directed to enter the bus with his hands behind his neck, among a group of 16 men. Two men were left behind. None were permitted to sit down. "17. Together with the other 15 men, four Serb soldiers armed with automatic weapons entered the bus. The bus proceeded and stopped a short time later. At this time the witness referred to Exhibit number 176, which is a map, with a yellow dot indicating the location -- a location near the dot where the bus stopped and where there was a widening of the road with the river off to the right. "18. Sometime before noon on the 13th of July, the men were ordered off the bus and lined up against a fence or a guard rail. The men were then directed to proceed downhill away from the roadside toward a bank of the Jadar river. PW-112 was third in line. Once at the river bank, the men were lined up again, after which the soldiers, including one of the individuals known to PW-112, opened fire. PW-112 was struck from behind in the left hip and fell into the water. PW-112 was carried downstream while being continually fired upon. "19. Eventually, PW-112 was able to draw himself out of the water on to a meadow where he surveyed his injuries. He was bleeding heavily and had difficulty moving but managed to break off a branch of a tree to assist himself in walking. The witness referred to Exhibit number 182, showing the river bank, and also referred to Exhibit number is 83, showing the bullet wound to his hip." That concludes my summary at this point. If I may, Your Honours, I would like to further inquire of the witness with respect to certain information that I think is relevant to your assessment of his credibility and the testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before that can I have a small clarification. In paragraph 2, you said the witness was forced to separate but it was his decision in light of the situation and he was not forced by a Serb or somebody like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, the reference to force, Your Honour, refers to an involuntary action based upon the circumstances which he was confronted with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: May I inquire?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, are you presently employed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And without telling us what kind of work, or without telling us where you are employed, can you tell us what kind of work you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I work at a company putting together different pieces. This is part of the electronic industry and I'm a mechanic by trade.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And how long have you been employed in this capacity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since 2004. And before that, I was employed somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you presently live alone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I live with my family, with my wife and two children.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And for how long have you been married?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since 1989.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you tell us how old your children are presently, approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My older son is 16 and my younger son is 13 going on 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And at the time that you fled Srebrenica, can you tell us approximately how old they were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were five and two respectively, the younger was born in February of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: For how long had you lived in Srebrenica municipality before 11 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I lived there from the beginning of April 1992 until the fall of Srebrenica in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And prior to that, did you live in another municipality or town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before that, from 1979, I resided in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And for what reason in particular did you move to Srebrenica from Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For safety reasons. The town had already been emptied. There was no communication between Bratunac and Srebrenica. One could not travel from Bratunac to Srebrenica -- Bratunac to Srebrenica. That's why I decided to withdraw to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, in July of 1995, were you -- well, let me ask you this. Withdrawn. Prior to your move to Srebrenica, were you a member of the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before I moved to Srebrenica? No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you become a member of the armed forces following your move to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was the Territorial Defence, and I became a member of the Territorial Defence towards the end of April 1992, and I stayed a member until January 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: After January 1993, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was demobilised and I was engaged on civilian jobs in the municipality. I worked as a courier. And later on, up to the fall of Srebrenica, I was employed by the DutchBat.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, when you say you were employed by the DutchBat, in what capacity were you so employed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a worker doing cleaning and other menial jobs, tidying up after lunch and such things.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And for about how long did you do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the last three and a half months.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, with respect to your job working for the DutchBat, did you receive any kind of identification?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We received a card with our first and last name and photograph on it so that we could enter the DutchBat compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is that the same identification to which your testimony in the previous trial refers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. It's the same identification but we had other documents such as our personal ID cards from the former Yugoslavia and other documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd like to direct your attention to the evening hours of 10th of July 1995, if I may. On that day, and around that time, did you take any action with regard to securing your family's safety?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Could you tell us briefly what if anything you did in that regard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last workday with DutchBat was the 8th of July. They told us then not to come any more because the situation was getting worse. On the 10th, in the evening, or in the afternoon sometime, the Serbs shelled the upper part of town so people were already withdrawing towards the camp in Srebrenica. Panic had broken out and I went with my family, together, to the DutchBat compound. This were some soldiers there who sold me -- who saw me. I spoke German so they told me to follow them towards Potocari. An APC was driving in front and a column of people was walking behind the APC. We came to the place called Solotusa where one shell was then fired from the Caus hill and it fell on the left side of the road into a field. That's when they stopped me. People ran off to all the different houses that were around. Then later, they used communications to get in touch with someone and then we went to the auto school training area. They went to the right. They came out of the APC, and they were shielding themselves behind some containers and then they explained to us that they couldn't guarantee our safety any more. That's when I went to an acquaintance of mine and I spent sometime there and then in the evening, around 10 p.m., I went back to town.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: During the time that you were following this APC, were you with your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was carrying my younger son, and my wife was sometimes carrying and sometimes just leading the older son.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Approximately how far outside of Srebrenica did you get before the shell was fired from the hill of Caus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three and a half to four kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you walk that entire distance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And approximately where were you relative to the APC when the shell landed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a couple of metres behind the APC.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And approximately how far from the APC did the shell land?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some 200 to 300 metres into the field on the left side of the road and on the left side of the river.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And if you can, can you approximate for the Court the number of people that were actually following this APC?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you the exact number but it was between 300 to 500 people, perhaps more.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: After you were informed that your safety could no longer be guaranteed, did you return back to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I returned to Srebrenica, to the apartment where I was living. The building was full of people in the halls. There were also some acquaintances and some people that I didn't know in my own apartment. There were people in the hall, on the stairs, inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you discuss the prospect of leaving Srebrenica with those other people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at the time because nobody knew what was going to happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Had you considered staying in the town of Srebrenica or in the vicinity in the face of the Serb advance into that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everybody was waiting to see what the people who were in power would do, so it was expected but nobody expected that it would be as bad as it was. The next day we were in front of the post office. When the UN observers left the post office, there were some contacts. They were speaking with the Presidency, with the government, and then around 2.00 or 3.00 p.m. the decision was made to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, when you made the decision to leave, did you take into consideration -- well, what specifically did you take into consideration in making the determination that you needed to leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From death or based on earlier experiences with the Serbs, nobody could expect to break through or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When you say "based on earlier experiences with the Serbs," could you briefly tell us what you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were many factors. The very beginning of the war in 1992, when the people that we lived with turned about at one point, to a completely different direction and from my experiences with neighbours with whom I was on good terms before, they were saying we had to leave. We said why? And then in a conversation they would say, some people would come but nobody knew who would come. So you would lose confidence. They said it would be better for you to leave. So actually, one of the main reasons was actually that I left Bratunac, the municipality of Bratunac, to go to the municipality of Srebrenica. So because of all those things that were going on, it was actually all of those things that were the reason to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, when you refer to all of those things that are going on, are you referring specifically to things that were going on in Bratunac or other areas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's a leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krgovic. Would you like to respond to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I may have missed the nature of the objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you repeat your objection again, Mr. Krgovic, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Actually I see it, Judge. Yes, I can respond to that. I'm simply asking the witness what he's referring to because his answer was relatively vague. If you would like, I can rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, just rephrase the question. I think it can be done quickly, in the simplest of forms.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Whether you say -- when you refer to things that are were going on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What specifically are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Detaining people at the playground in Bratunac, the burning of surrounding villages, Glogova, Rance, Cerovac, Mihajlovici, and then from other people who managed to flee from those areas, to the municipality of Srebrenica area, we heard what was going on. These were the main reasons. The surrounding villages were burned. A lot of the population was expelled from this playing field to the -- in the direction of Tuzla. It was conversations with the people who fled other areas to come to the Srebrenica area. Detention at the playing field, calling out people who had some money on them or calling out of influential people. Things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Had you had the opportunity to discuss those matters with other people in your community before the 11th of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you say whether or not in your estimation these events were generally well known in your community?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I spoke with people who had fled, and whom some Serbs left when they caught them in the bus, in the village of Rance, because they recognised some of them, even though they had stockings on their head. We couldn't believe ourselves that these people that we were on good terms with ended up killing. The reasons to leave Srebrenica in 1995 were quite important reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, having worked at the DutchBat base, did you have a fair amount of contact with those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. With some of them who spoke some German. We spoke when they were in the bar or we played billiards sometimes during a break. With those who wanted to be in contact.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And when you decided to leave Srebrenica on the 11th of July 1995, did you do so at the behest of the DutchBat soldiers or at the behest of UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Not specifically, but the actual belief of the people who were supposed to offer us protection, they were unable to do that, and then the experience that I had with the ID that I had from them, and the fact that they could not protect me, and if they couldn't, what could I do then? There were people who also worked in Potocari, I don't want to mention them, who didn't come, and others.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Your Honours, for the next part of my examination, I would request if we could go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session for a while, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: At this point, Your Honours, I just wanted to introduce some additional exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to have the witness shown 65 ter number 1618, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Sorry, Judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, have you had an opportunity to see this photograph before today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you tell us what's depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see the crossroads at Konjevic Polje and you can see the bridge leading to Kasaba. You can also see where the Kravica River flows into the Jadar River.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recall seeing a photograph, this particular photograph, prior to today, in my office?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Could I have called up, please, P02274?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. What's the problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I was just wondering if the photograph could be rotated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But I --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I have a hard copy of the photograph. It might be faster just to put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I rotated mine already.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Could we make it a little bit bigger so that the witness could have a good look at it? Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recognise that document, sir? That photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, do you see a marking on that photograph, a circle?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would object to the witness being shown a photograph that's previously been marked. I thought we went over this earlier. I thought photographs were supposed to be put in front of witnesses clean and let them mark them and I object to this -- the way they are doing this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I also noticed, Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I support that objection and I also did Mr. Vanderpuye the courtesy of informing him that I would object to this on Friday afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So Mr. Vanderpuye, what's your position on this? Who marked -- is this the witness's same marking?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I was just about to put the question to him. The answer is yes. And I was about to put the question to him to see if he could identify the markings that are on the photograph and elicit from him the circumstances, the time or the location in which those markings were made by him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is this witness, as marked, was -- sorry, was this photo, as marked, used in the previous proceedings?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In the Krstic trial?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: M'hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No, it was not. It's a new exhibit and it's predicated on 65 ter number 1618 which was shown to him initially.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, do you recognise the markings that are depicted on the photo that's now before you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I made this marking.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And did you make these markings prior to today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Were those markings made in my office?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what are those markings meant to depict or to show on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is where the agricultural storage depot was before the war, and during the war. Now there is a gas station there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is this a fair and accurate depiction of the intersection of Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Skip that. I think you covered that in your previous question.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Very well. Okay. I'd also like to have another exhibit shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm sorry, but frankly, I can't see any markings on the photograph in front of me. Maybe he could point it out with the pen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Fair enough. I mean, I can. But if you can't, then obviously -- yeah. Could you mark an arrow pointing to the markings that in your mind Mr. Vanderpuye has just referred you to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'd like to know if counsel would be able to blow up their picture on their own.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, we cannot do that. On the middle screen here, we get -- we see what we get.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Judge Kwon. Witness, please place an arrow pointing to the markings on that photo that Mr. Vanderpuye asked you a question about a few minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the part here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. It's okay. It's not an arrow but I can live with it. Is it okay for you now, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And if you look carefully you will notice the outline of the previous circle in blue. All right. Thank you. Your next question, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I had -- well let me ask the witness the following:

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you see a church in that photograph? And that is referring to P02274, the photograph before you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And was that church there at around the time that you've indicated you were at that location in 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That church was built in 1997 or 1998. I never knew that there was a church here before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could the witness put a mark, put PW-112 next to that red circle that he's put on the photo, please? PW- ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, I didn't quite understand what I'm supposed to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Write "PW-112" next to that circle.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd like to have the witness shown 65 ter 1935, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What do you recognise that photograph to be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the house where we were kept for a brief period of time after the interrogation.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And is that the house to which you referred in your prior testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is it a fair and accurate depiction of the building in which you were held for a brief period of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I would like to have the witness shown P02275, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, we finally have it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recognise this photograph, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what do you recognise this photograph to be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the house and two trees in front of the house where we were interrogated by men wearing uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is this the house to which your prior testimony refers as the side of the interrogation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in front of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is it a fair and accurate depiction of the house as you recall it having been in 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Could I have the witness shown, please, 65 ter number 1924?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is there a way of speeding this up? It's very slow.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recognise this photograph, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is my wound, the wound on my body.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is this the wound to which you referred in your prior testimony that you gave on 23 May 2000?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: This is the bullet wound you received during the time of the execution on 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you indicate on the photograph from which direction the bullet entered and from which direction the bullet exited?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is where it entered. And this is where it exited.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Please -- could you please initial the photograph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just put PW-112, "P" for papa, "W" for whiskey, 112.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And could you put the number 1 for the entry and the number 2 for the exit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I have nothing further at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Does the original of this photo -- is the original of this photo black and white or does it exist in colour? Do you know, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Maybe I can ask the witness, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, do you know, sir, whether or not the original of this photograph is in black and white or it's in colour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know. This was done here at the Tribunal, and I believe that this is the original because the last time I saw it it was also black and white.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Judge, I will make a determination as to whether it -- the indication is it's a Polaroid photograph, so it's likely in colour, but I will find that out and get that information to the Court as soon as I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Mr. Vanderpuye. I take it there are no further questions from the Prosecution, which means we are now going to start with the series of cross-examinations.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have changed the order of the cross-examination, so the Defence of General Gvero is going to be first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Mr. Zivanovic. Witness, it's Mr. Krgovic, who is lead counsel for General Gvero and he will be the first one to cross-examine you. May I just have a very quick indication where we stand? How long do you think you're cross-examination will last?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Half an hour, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And then Mr. Zivanovic? The same?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That's one hour and Mr. Meek or Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Judge, since the schedule has changed, it maybe half an hour or no questions. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. That's one hour and a half. Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, definitely less than 30 minutes, if any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's okay. Ms. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A quarter of an hour, if any at all. It will depend on the previous cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Mr. Haynes?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Miracles do happen. Yes, Mr. Krgovic, sorry for having interrupted you like that but please go ahead. We'll have a break at 10.30 or thereabouts, depending on when it's more convenient for you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I'll try and put questions to you so as to enable you to answer by just yes or no, but I would kindly ask you to pause before answering since we speak the same language and we need to be interpreted for everybody in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In addition to your previous testimony, you have provided several statements to this Tribunal and also you provided statements to the organs of security in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In your testimony before this Tribunal, which you confirmed on examination-in-chief, you said that you were a member of the TO in 1992 until the end of 1993. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Beginning of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: After that, you were in charge of being a liaison officer between the civilian organs and the front line in Srebrenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown Exhibit 5D84?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This is page 1. Do you remember having provided this statement to the Prosecutor's Office of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown page 1 of this document? In other words, the following page of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, look at paragraph 1 and look at the last sentence in that paragraph, I'm going to read it to you. "I was a courier between the civilian authorities and the defence lines." Do you remember having stated that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a mistranslation. I was a courier in a department of the municipality of Srebrenica and I did not perform any courier services between the lines and the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, you were a member of the Secretariat for National Defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Of the Srebrenica municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: What was your job?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a courier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And the fact that you maintained contact between the municipality and defence lines is actually not correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: After those days around the 10th of July, you were aware of the developments around Srebrenica, once the attack had started on Srebrenica, and you had information as to what was going on; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown Exhibit number 5D82?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, you provided a statement to the higher court in Tuzla on the 2nd of August 1995. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Is this your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I prefer to be extra cautious rather than take risks. Please stop, stop, stop, stop, stop. Private session, no broadcasting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Mr. Krgovic, as usual, please use your good judgement, exercise the greatest caution as you proceed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In the meantime, do we have English translation of these documents? Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Krgovic, again my apologies for the interruption. Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, look at the sentence in the upper part where it says, "First they took up the UNPROFOR check-point at green Jadar, the UNPROFOR had withdrawn from there leaving the materiel and technical supplies. That's why the army was forced to take up the position above the green Jadar and maintained it for a few days." Do you remember that part of your statement given to the Court in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe in a different forum. This statement is full of mistakes. I was hospitalised at the time and I was forced to give that statement, and these are not the only mistakes. There are a lot of things that I don't agree with in this statement. I signed it there, but I would like to answer other questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Who forced you to give that statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people who were in charge of collecting information from the victims of war and from the survivors.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Let me draw your attention to the bottom of the page, the sentence starts with the following words: "All the men were told to start moving towards Susnjari because the --"

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the statement was signed by the witness and the signature is visible at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. It's okay. As long as this is not being broadcast, we do not have a problem because I understand this is just for our convenience. But the important thing is that there are no people in the public gallery that can visibly read your -- what you have on your monitors, which I don't think is the case today, and otherwise you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Word was circulated that all men should go towards Susnjari where there would be an assembly point. Women, children and the old were to go to the UNPROFOR base at Potocari where UNPROFOR should have provided them with protection. It was agreed that we should leave Susnjari in a column and small groups and go through the Chetnik lines towards Tuzla." Is this how things transpired at the moment when it was decided that all the men would start moving towards Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody made that decision. A majority of the men started moving towards Slatina and Susnjari. The plan was to try and break through towards Tuzla and this was the only route that one could take to get there eventually.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: As for this decision, was this communicated to you by the president of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, when you arrived in Susnjari, a group was formed, led by the president of the municipality, Osman Suljic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not just Osman Suljic, everybody else who worked at the municipality was there and the group was not formed. Some 12.000 to 15.000 people arrived there. Some had already passed through the Serb lines. Nothing was formed. People just arrived there from all over the place, from the direction of Potocari, Bljeceva, Slatina and other villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And Osman Suljic was the leader of the group in which you moved?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown Exhibit number 5D83?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you remember that you provided this statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be shown the last page of this statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I signed this statement but there is another one that you might show later which I never provided. I did provide this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did the events described in this statement reflect your best recollection at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was an August, when I was discharged from the hospital. I don't agree with all the details in this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown page 3 in this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, could you please look at the sentence at the top of the page. It says: "That my group was led by Osman", and then part was redacted. "The president of the municipality of Srebrenica. In that group there were also my and the names are mentioned, of the people who were in that group." Do you remember having stated that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The column was from Susnjari to Buljim which is about two or three kilometres. I did not manage to leave Susnjari from 12 midnight until 5.00 in the morning, so you can imagine how long the column was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I'm just asking you whether Osman Suljic led your group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody led the group. We just walked one after another.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, maybe this would be a convenient time for our first break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. Krgovic. We will have a 25-minute break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We continue. We are informed that the Prosecution, to what Mr. McCloskey -- Mr. Nicholls, have asked for an extension of the time for filing the proofing chart from the 30th -- 31st of October, which is the date we had fixed, way back, to the 10th of November. We are also informed by our Senior Legal Officer, Mr. Cubbon that there is no objection on the part of the Defence teams. I take it that is confirmed. Yes. I hear no objections there. So yes, we are granting the extension to the 10th of November, Mr. McCloskey. Thank you. The other thing I wanted to know is that in preparing our decisions on the protective measure motions, the two motions that we very briefly touched upon last Friday, it's not clear to us if, when you stood up, Ms. Nikolic, you answered or you gave the green light in relation to both motions or whether it was restricted only to one of the motions. If you could clarify that, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. It referred to only one of those requests for Witnesses 50 and 54, the motion was submitted on Friday for the current week. The other requests we will be able to let you know during the course of today or tomorrow. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you so much. So that confirms what I thought. So let's proceed with the witness, please. Thank you. Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to continue. Do you remember my last question, which you answered? And it was whether Osman Suljic was there. Did you see him that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In front of the post office and around the post office, yes, but later, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Suljic was wearing a camouflage uniform and he had a weapon, do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that according to testimonies before this Trial Chamber, he went for meetings with UNPROFOR that day and he was walking around in a camouflage uniform with a weapon, would that lead to you change anything in what you said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, does that mean that this sentence, which I read out to you before the break, that Osman Suljic was the president of the municipality of Srebrenica and that he was leading your group, was incorrect?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you sign this statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever, when you talked with the representatives from the Prosecutor's Office, and the investigators, when you were submitting corrections, did you ask that that part be corrected?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And was this done?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When I showed you your previous statement given to the investigators of this Tribunal, when you spoke about your position, did you, when the statement was read back to you, point to that mistake?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this was a mistake in the translation, a courier between the civilian and the military authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness again look at document 5D84, both versions, English and the B/C/S version? The next page, please. And in English, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, make sure there is no broadcast of this; okay? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to read it to you in English, what it states in the English version of your statement. "I was a courier between the civilian authorities and the lines of defence." [Interpretation] I don't see any mistakes in the translation between -- in these two statements. And investigator Ruez who took this statement, did you indicate this difference to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The statement was given and the interpreter or the translator was from Croatia, and you know that there are some words and this happened on Friday too, that they are different from one testimony to the next. In one case, I said "water basin" and they said the basin for bathing. And these are the kinds of mistakes that we encountered. So I think it is a question of translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, when you came to Susnjari, you were lined up by your leadership into lines and groups were formed in such a way that there were people there who were armed and those who were not armed; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Each group left at a precise time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't a group. It was a column.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: But groups were formed and these groups were mixed, including armed and unarmed people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This happened the next day. People who stayed behind, people who didn't manage to pass through the first Serb lines at Budjim.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So this is not correct, that part of your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's not true that groups were formed in Susnjari but people returned to Buljim the next day to try to take people across who were without weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So that part of the statement, which was introduced as an exhibit before the Trial Chamber and which you confirmed to the Prosecutor as being correct, now is not correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, do you know what the distance is from Susnjari to Budjim?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I'm only asking you about this part because, in your testimony which was admitted as an exhibit before this Trial Chamber, that's what it stated, so I just want to know if you abide by what you said now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, sir, as a courier, in the Territorial Defence, and as liaison between the municipal defence organ and the front line, were a member of the Srebrenica armed forces; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From 1993, I was in the civilian sector, as a courier. I had nothing to do with the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about 1995. In July 1995, you, as a courier, maintained links between the Territorial Defence in Srebrenica and the front line and as such, were a member of the Srebrenica armed forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: And where were these lines?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would register an objection with Mr. Krgovic's line of questioning at this point because I think it assumes facts that aren't in evidence. There hasn't been any testimony that he served in that capacity during that period of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, what are you basing your line of questions upon? I think that there is an affirmation from the witness himself at some point in time that he was indeed a courier, but that's about it. I think we can live with the line of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I respond, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The way we recollect, and I think it's a good recollection, is that the witness has confirmed that he was a courier, yes, there is no question about that, but he has also confirmed that he was not crossing the -- crossing the lines while he was doing that. So please, then, restrict yourself to what he has confirmed and try to avoid repeating -- avoid repetition basically but otherwise feel free to ask him whatever you like, as related to his role of courier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my line of questioning is related to his statement and this last sentence in this document in front of us where he says that he was a courier between the civilian authorities and the line of defence. And I am putting it to the witness that according to that, he was a member of the armed forces. I just want him to answer yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I was not a member of the armed forces in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, none of these documents, and these excerpts from the documents that I have shown to you, are incorrect. Do you still abide by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: How do you mean that they are not correct? What is correct is that I was not in the liberation forces as of January 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Since I asked you about the statement, I'm just summing up, as for each of these statements, parts of the statements that I showed to you, you said that these parts are not correct. Do you abide by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The statements that I provided earlier, yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And this last part, when you testified about these groups, and that's already in the transcript of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I answered that. These were not groups. It was a column.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So that part is incorrect as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Mr. Krgovic. Mr. Zivanovic, who is appearing for Colonel Popovic, will now proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Please clarify one thing for me. Normally once somebody is admitted in a hospital, the doctors ask you about your condition, how you feel, what your complaints are and whether you are injured, whether you suffer any pain and similar things. Was that the case with you when you were admitted in this surgery on the 16th of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct. But that's a normal situation. However, the situation was not normal. There were a lot of wounded people being brought by private cars, private lorries. I had to wait for two hours to be admitted, so you can assume what the situation was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I can assume that. Did they ask you about your particulars, your name, your last name, the date of birth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You provided them that, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I suppose that they also asked you whether you were a soldier or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Gradina, no, they never asked me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean Gradina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm referring to the clinical center of Gradina with several hospital facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did they ask you if you were a courier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they never did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: So you believe that they put it in just like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was inserted later at the garrison ambulance.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And that's when you were asked about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you another thing. On the 27th of July, 1995, at the garrison, surgery, you were visited by a person whom you didn't know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And he introduced himself as somebody from the 2nd Corps of the BiH army, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. If you tell me his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at Exhibit 5D89. Can we go to page 3 of this document, please. Do you recognise this statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No broadcast.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please give me the name, who that is from? This is my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: At the very beginning you will see that on the 27th of July, 1995, you were visited by a man who was brought by a nurse and that he introduced himself to you as somebody representing the 2nd Corps that works with journalists. Is that what you stated? Is that what you wrote?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You also stated that he wore a black shirt with the insignia of the BiH army. Can you see that in the next sentence, two lines further down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You can remember, then. And later on you say that he told you that you should provide a false testimony and say that you were wounded in Karakaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This was my Smajo Elezovic and I didn't want to give him a statement and there was a conflict between him and me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And that was the person who had visited you. His name was Smajo Elezovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And then you stated this. I don't know whether you can see it. It says here he asked me to provide a statement since I -- since he had heard that I was one of the survivors in the group that had been taken to execution, he asked me in the corridor how I survived? And I told him how that happened. Are you reading?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And then he asked me to say that I was a member of the group who had been taken for execution in Karakaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was Smajo Elezovic. He wanted me to provide that statement but I didn't want to give it to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: But you refused that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: So he did ask you to provide a statement that you had been taken for execution in Karakaj?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please slow down and you slow down and allow a short pause between question and answer because you're going too fast for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me just repeat. I don't know what has been interpreted. In other words, you confirm that this is what he asked you to do but you refused?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: That's all I have. No further questions for this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Mr. Zivanovic. Who is next? Mr. Meek? Mr. Meek is together with Mr. Ostojic, representing Colonel Beara here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. How are you today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You may not know this but I have received a supplemental information sheet dated the 26th of October 2006, from the Office of the Prosecutor, from Mr. Vanderpuye, who proofed you. The Prosecutor is to your right. Did you have a chance to have that read to you in your own language? It's the supplemental information sheet you provided us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to my statement? Or my testimony in the Krstic case?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes. Both. In both.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This was not in B/C/S. It was in English, but it was read back to me in B/C/S. And this was my mistake that I made on Friday. That was the confusion on Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we are still somewhat in the midst of a confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: We are at cross-purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly at the moment you mentioned also the testimony, transcript of the Krstic, that did it. So you also need to explain to him what you're talking about. Because he'll probably -- doesn't know what the proofing briefs are.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: After you met with Mr. Vanderpuye on the 26th of October, the 25th of October, last week -- I'm not sure whether you met him one day or two days. Can you tell me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two days.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: After that, Mr. Vanderpuye had generated a two-page document stating all kinds of inconsistencies that you told him about from your prior testimony and your prior statements. So my question to you: Did anybody read that two-page statement back to you about the various inconsistencies in your prior statements and in your prior testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: All right. Well, I want to ask you briefly about your testimony in the Krstic case and that would be 23 May 2000. And first you do recall testifying in that case, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And on page 3267 of that transcript, you were discussing being placed in a warehouse. Do you recall that testimony generally?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I think you ought to repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge. I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You were captured by the -- some Serb police officers, but yet you failed to utilise the hand grenade which you stated was -- you had with you only for one purpose, and that is to not be captured, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Correct. I didn't have the time to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: All right. And you'll agree with me that before you left on your march through the woods, to the free territory, medicine was limited, supplies of medicine was very limited in Srebrenica; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was practically none. There was no supply whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And yet, can you explain to this Tribunal, this Trial Chamber, why it is that you had medicine on you along with that grenade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because I worked for the DutchBat and I got a few dressings from a soldier and some other things.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Well, you had more than just bandaids in your bag, didn't you? Didn't you have medicine for pain or to stop the bleeding?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were just ampules for injections.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. So you had injectable medicine with you in your bag. Did you have the syringes to inject it also, in case you needed to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And you received these from the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, did you not, or members thereof?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Now, in your prior statements, and in your prior testimony, you indicated a reference to when you were captured and you were on the road. Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And as you were speaking with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, sorry to interrupt you, Mr. Meek. I think it's the case of distinguishing between the grenade, the hand grenade, and the medical items. Because you asked a very direct question which you are entitled to, whether he got the medicine from the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And he gave a straightforward answer, no, which could be interpreted as meaning that that applies also to the hand grenade. So perhaps you can distinguish between one and the other and put two questions instead of one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Judge. And I think he has answered the question about the medicine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But I think we need to have it clear in the transcript. But I know what he said but we need to clarify that Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness, you just answered a question that you did not receive the medicine, the injectable medicine or the syringes from the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina or any member thereof. Is that correct? You did not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-112 [Resumed]
